newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close higher on frost forecasts.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close higher on frost forecasts.

text.p: CBOT soybeans closed higher on forecasts for frost early next week in portions of the U.S. Midwest, traders said.

"It was a little oversold and there are still the frost fears. But it's still a waiting game to see what happens and we're just going back and forth," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
Several meteorologists early Friday said there was a possibility for frost early next week in the northern portion of the U.S. Midwest.
There also was talk of another freeze late in the week.
Rosenthal Collins bought three million bushels of November and funds and commission houses purchased from one half to one million bushels of November, the traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 45,000 contracts, down from 65,792 Thursday, according to the CBOT.
Soybean futures closed five to seven cents per bushel higher, with November up six at $7.95-1/4 a bushel.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 18,000, down from 26,756 Thursday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Produce Grain bought 600 November $8.00 calls and sold 600 November $8.25 calls at 8-1/2 cents. Lind Waldock bought 500 November $8.25 calls at 10-1/4 cents and Rosenthal Collins bought 300 November $8.00 calls at 18-1/2 to 19-1/2 cents, traders said.
